selected_evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections
selected_evidence.summary: The persistent change succeeded; after reboot, firewalld remained enabled and active with TCP 22/8080 accept rules followed by an administrative reject. Direct ingress tests connected to ports 22 and 8080 while port 8081 was rejected.

selected_evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel retained
selected_evidence.summary: Both before and after configuration/restart, node1 reports AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID f38484ef-a289-4d30-9a94-4ab42c44f900 was captured; systemd acknowledged the safe reboot; recovered boot ID b0338da3-5723-4734-885c-a7cdea6e1f73 proves restart. Post-restart checks show the system running, SSH and firewalld active, persistent/live policy restored, and expected traffic behavior.

	}

commands.command: nft -a list chain inet firewalld filter_IN_public_allow; command -v ip; command -v python3

bash -s <<'FWTEST'
set -eu
cleanup() {
  [ -n "${srv_pid:-}" ] && kill "$srv_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  firewall-cmd --zone=public --remove-interface=veth-fw >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  ip link del veth-fw 2>/dev/null || true
  ip netns del fwprobe 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT
ip netns add fwprobe
ip link add veth-fw type veth peer name veth-ns
ip link set veth-ns netns fwprobe
ip addr add 198.18.0.1/30 dev veth-fw
ip link set veth-fw up
ip netns exec fwprobe ip addr add 198.18.0.2/30 dev veth-ns
ip netns exec fwprobe ip link set lo up
ip netns exec fwprobe ip link set veth-ns up
firewall-cmd --zone=public --add-interface=veth-fw >/dev/null
python3 -c 'import socket,time
socks=[]
for p in (8080,8081):
 s=socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); s.bind(("198.18.0.1",p)); s.listen(2); socks.append(s)
time.sleep(15)' &
srv_pid=$!
sleep 1
ip netns exec fwprobe python3 - <<'PY'
import socket
for port in (8080, 8081):
    sock = socket.socket()
    sock.settimeout(3)
    try:
        sock.connect(('198.18.0.1', port))
        print('tcp/%d: CONNECTED' % port)
    except OSError as exc:
        print('tcp/%d: REJECTED (%s)' % (port, exc))
    finally:
        sock.close()
PY
FWTEST
